turns.response_html:
The main "stairway" to YouTube Shorts is the dedicated Shorts tab at the bottom of the YouTube mobile app or on the side menu on a desktop browser.

  • On the App: Look for the "Shorts" button at the bottom of the screen.
  • On a PC: Find "Shorts" in the menu on the side.

You can also find Shorts on the homepage, on channel pages, and in search results.

Would you like to know how to create your own YouTube Short?

turns.prompt_text: is there a way to have you too shorts go to the next short via voice command or a timer
turns.response_html:
No, YouTube does not have a built-in voice command or a timer to automatically advance to the next Short.

However:

  • Third-party extensions/apps (like Chrome extensions or other auto-scroll apps) exist for desktop and mobile to automatically advance to the next Short when the current one ends.
  • You can set up custom voice commands using your phone's accessibility features (like Voice Control on iPhone or similar features on Android) to mimic a "swipe up" to advance to the next Short.
  • The keyboard shortcut for the next track (Shift+N on desktop) can sometimes advance the Short.

Would you like steps on how to set up a custom voice command on your phone to scroll?

You can use your phone's accessibility settings to create a voice command that mimics the "swipe up" motion to scroll to the next Short.

📱 For iPhone (Using Voice Control)

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control.
  2. Toggle on Voice Control.
  3. Go to Customize Commands > Custom > Create New Command.
  4. For the Phrase, type the word you want to say (e.g., "Next").
  5. Tap Action > Run Custom Gesture.
  6. On the screen, quickly swipe up once, then tap Save.
  7. Tap Save again to save the new command.
  8. Now, when Voice Control is active and you are watching Shorts, say your chosen phrase (e.g., "Next") to scroll.

🤖 For Android (Using Voice Access)

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Voice Access.
  2. Enable Voice Access and follow the setup/tutorial.
  3. Once active, you can simply use built-in commands like "Scroll up" or "Swipe up" to move to the next Short. For some custom actions, you may need to use the "Voice Access Commands" setting to customize gestures, but the default scroll commands often work for Shorts.
